messages.author: cac7de606a15cc66
messages.subject: Dynamic Tobit model in Stan
parts:
Hi all, I am trying to implement in Stan a generalization of the Tobit model, a dynamic Tobit model with lagged observed variables. 
My core idea is that of trying to model the soccer players performances (ratings) over the season through the previous performance (lagged dependent  variable) and a bunch of predictors.  The final aim is to be able - in a rough way - to do some predictions and to test the goodness of the model with cross validation and elppd approach. So far, a simple AR(1) varying-intercept hierarchical model - with as many groups as the different players positions in the field and without predictors except the intercepts - gives good results in terms of fitting and of Rhat. Since for every player a censored value arises whenever the player doesn't play - i.e., when his performance is not observed - i need to move towards a model that is able to deal with it, and the dynamic Tobit seems to be suitable for this objective.     

However, the main computational problem - as I outline in the attached pdf file - stems from the fact that there is not a closed form for the likelihood, since this would require an integral with as many dimension as censored times. In the literature (you can find the reference in the pdf file) a simulated likelihood approach is proposed, and I am trying to implement this in Stan.

In the attached Stan file you find the draft of the model. Just for being clearer about my code:

- t are the data, the ratings of the players (values bounded between 1 and 15), collected for N (around 300) players and for L (around 20) games.
- eta_error are the generated truncated normal random variables, epsilon are  Uniform(0,1) random variables
- Phi_factor regard the  contributes for the simulated likelihood, for the observed and for the censored times.
- so far, the eta_error component is not still included in the "oberved likelihood  part", as the general procedure of Chang would suggest.

I launch the Stan model with these settings:

fanta_stan_dyn_tobit<-stan(file="dynamicTobit5.stan",data=fanta_dat_dyn_tobit, 
                           iter=1000,
                           init="0",init_r=0,
                           control=list(adapt_delta=0.9, max_treedepth=12),
                           chains=3, cores=3,verbose = FALSE)

As results, with this code I have several divergent transitions after warmup (500 for each chain), terrible mixing, high Rhat and , even with a smaller dataset with  N = 15 and L= 7 the code speeds up slowly.
I suspect that the specification for the scale parameters could be wrong, but from the original paper of Chang-Sheng-Kai it is not straightforward understand how to properly model them (I force them to be between 0 and 1).
I don't know why, but if in lines 60- 61 of the Stan file I set up the truncation with the following:

increment_log_prob(normal_log(eta_error[r, n, l-1], 0, 1));
      increment_log_prob(normal_cdf(trunc_point, 0, 1));   

without the "-" (as written in the reference manual and as it seems to me obvious), my inference gets better, with more reasonable results (in some sense close to the simple AR(1) varying intercept model) and with Rhat much more close to 1.1...I don't grab this behaviour, maybe I am doing some mathematical mistakes with the truncation.

So far I tried to:
- change priors, use the "Matt tricks"
- Use sampling statement, with the T[,] for truncations.
- Reparametrize the model. 

Anyway, thank you in advance for your patience. I am managing with this problem for a while, feel free to tell me if and what doesn't makes sense.
I appreciate any advice.
Thanks

Leonardo

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Dynamic Tobit model in Stan
parts:
If someone doesn't play, can't you just have an unobserved
latent ability at that time as part of the model?

Or is there a way to only deal with the observed games in
the likelihood, but have the variance somehow depend on time
so that if there's a bigger time between games, there might be
a bigger difference in ability?

Usually forcing parameters into a constrained interval if
they are not physically constrained (like probabilities) is
a bad idea. It's easy for the real answer to want to be outside
the interval and force all the probability mass against the boundaries
and present both statistical and computational problems.

> I don't know why, but if in lines 60- 61 of the Stan file I set up the truncation with the following:
>
> increment_log_prob(normal_log(eta_error[r, n, l-1], 0, 1));
> increment_log_prob(normal_cdf(trunc_point, 0, 1));
>
> without the "-" (as written in the reference manual and as it seems to me obvious),

You probably want the CDF on the log scale, normal_cdf_log(...).
If it's truncation below a point, it's just -normal_cdf_log(...) (the
negation being because it's in the denominator and we're working in
the log domain).

- Bob

>If someone doesn't play, can't you just have an unobserved

I have to think about it, maybe yes. If I got it what you mean, you suggest to have just a random variable with a specified distribution whenever the player doesn't play, right? Maybe this could ease the likelihood specification, which in this case could be more similar to a simple Tobit model.

>Or is there a way to only deal with the observed games in
>the likelihood, but have the variance somehow depend on time
>so that if there's a bigger time between games, there might be
>a bigger difference in ability?

This is for sure interesting, and maybe yields a change of mind of the model. I want to think on it. If so, maybe the whole structure could be similar to a simpler AR(1) hierarchical model (that I firstly used), with a variance structure which would somehow depend on time. In this case, I wouldn't require a simulation procedure for the likelihood

>You probably want the CDF on the log scale, normal_cdf_log(...).
>If it's truncation below a point, it's just -normal_cdf_log(...) (the
>negation being because it's in the denominator and we're working in

In the meanwhile, thanks Bob for your useful suggestions. If you have any other, glad to hear it.

Leonardo
